hook_text: Cereal box, tin of beans, an orange. Three breakfast things, three solid shapes, and none of them is a square or a circle.
clip_script: Open the kitchen cupboard. Cereal box: six flat faces, all rectangles, twelve edges, eight corners. A rectangular prism. Tin of beans: two circles at the ends and a curved surface round the middle. A cylinder. It rolls on its side but stands on its end. An orange: curved all over, no faces, no edges, no corners. A sphere. Not a circle, because a circle is flat and you cannot peel it. Now step outside to Egypt: a square base, four triangles leaning in to one point. A square pyramid, five faces. The box and the tin are the same all the way through. The pyramid narrows to a point. The ball is curved everywhere. Four objects, four questions: curved all over, two circles and a curve, six rectangles, or a base with triangles to a point. Name the solid, not the flat shape on its side.
visual_style: Whiteboard cupboard with each object pulled out and its faces highlighted one by one; a pyramid sliced into shrinking squares.
pacing: Three objects named with their parts, the pyramid contrast, then the four-question rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find a prism, a cylinder and a sphere in your own kitchen.
